title: Submission metadata can link the student across courses and submissions
description: The flow carries student id, course, work file, and submission timestamp together. At the receiving web app, these attributes enable linking multiple submissions by the same student across courses and over time, creating a longitudinal activity profile.
assumptions: The portal stores or can observe repeated submissions associated with the same student identifier.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement because the retrieved context only confirms applicability of threat types to ExternalEntity->Process flows, not detailed node ids.

title: Student identity is exposed to the portal through direct identifiers in the submission flow
description: The submission includes a student id and course context, directly identifying the student to the receiving process. If the portal or its operators do not need the full identifier at this stage, the flow reveals more identity information than necessary.
assumptions: The student id is a direct identifier and is visible to the receiving application and potentially administrators or logs.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine identifiability concern on the receiving process, but exact threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Student may be unable to deny a submission because the portal records attributable evidence
description: By receiving the work file together with student id and submission timestamp, the portal can create evidence tying a specific student to a specific submission event. This can remove plausible deniability if students were not informed that such attributable records would be retained or used.
assumptions: The portal logs or stores the submission event with identity and timestamp.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is included because the flow naturally creates attributable records; applicability depends on retention and evidentiary use.

title: The submission flow reveals sensitive academic activity
description: The combination of course, assignment file contents, student id, and submission timestamp discloses that the student is enrolled in or participating in a particular course and reveals academic work and timing behavior. File contents may also contain additional personal data beyond what is necessary for upload handling.
assumptions: Assignment files may contain personal content or embedded metadata; course participation is considered personal information.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; disclosure clearly applies to this flow.

title: The portal may process more submission data than necessary for the stated purpose
description: Receiving the full work file, student id, course, and precise submission timestamp may exceed what is strictly necessary if, for example, pseudonymous submission, coarser timestamps, or minimized metadata would suffice. Embedded document metadata may further increase data volume beyond the intended purpose.
assumptions: No explicit data-minimization controls strip unnecessary metadata or reduce identifier precision before receipt.
uncertainty_note: This threat is grounded in data minimization concerns at collection/receipt; exact node id is approximate.

title: Students may not understand what submission metadata and file metadata are collected
description: From the student's perspective, it may be unclear that the portal receives not only the visible assignment file and entered fields, but also precise timestamps and potentially hidden document metadata. This can undermine transparency about the scope of personal data collection on submission.
assumptions: The interface or privacy notice does not clearly explain all collected fields and metadata.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is plausible for this flow, but depends on the portal's notices and UI disclosures.

title: Collection of identifiable submission data may lack a clear lawful basis or exceed stated privacy commitments
description: The portal collects identifiable academic submissions and associated metadata. If the system lacks an appropriate legal basis, fails to honor purpose limitation, or retains/uses the data beyond assignment handling and grading, the collection on this flow may be non-compliant with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable education/privacy regulations or institutional policies require necessity, transparency, and purpose limitation for this collection.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction, institutional policy, and actual notices/retention practices; included because the flow clearly involves personal data collection.

title: Assignment service processes directly identified student data
description: The flow includes student id together with course and role, so the assignment & grading service processes data tied to an identified or readily identifiable student. This creates an identifying threat because the service receives and handles identified data rather than a less identifying alternative.
assumptions: Student id is unique within the institution and can be linked to a specific student by P2 or connected systems.

title: Unique student identifier is transmitted to the grading service
description: The transmitted student id is a unique reference to the data subject. Its presence in this process-to-process flow increases identifiability of the submission and grading request at P2.

title: Potential over-disclosure of personal data in routed grading requests
description: The portal forwards student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the assignment & grading service.
